note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following recent biopsy confirmation of high-grade prostate cancer.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a retired warehouse worker, married, and lives alone, with his spouse as the primary contact. He has a history of hypertension managed with amlodipine and valsartan, and is an ex-smoker who quit in 2005. He reports moderate LUTS with an IPSS score of 12/35, but denies any bone pain or haematuria. He enjoys hiking on weekends and consumes no alcohol. Recent PSA trend shows a sharp rise from 1.1 ng/mL in March 2024 to 70.0 ng/mL in February 2025.

On DRE, the prostate is normal in consistency and symmetry, consistent with cT1c staging. General examination reveals stable vital signs with BP 137/95 mmHg and HR 66 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or signs of metastatic disease are observed.
